stem: Meena watches the night sky from her terrace in Jaipur. She notices that the Pole Star seems to stay in almost the same place all night, while the other stars seem to move around it. Why does the Pole Star appear nearly stationary?

options.text: Earth revolves around the Sun, so the stars make circular trails around the Pole Star
Earth's rotation axis points very close to the Pole Star, so it appears nearly fixed while other stars seem to move around it
The other stars orbit the Pole Star, so only they appear to move
The Pole Star is the nearly stationary centre of star trails in both the northern and southern hemispheres

teacher.key_rationale: The Pole Star appears nearly stationary because Earth's rotation axis points almost directly at it; Earth's rotation makes other stars trace apparent circular paths around it. Option A wrongly credits revolution around the Sun, C wrongly claims other stars orbit the Pole Star, and D wrongly extends visibility of the Pole Star as a fixed centre to both hemispheres.
